articles.title: USWNT returnees earn 2-2 draw against Spain, an early World Cup wake-up call
articles.summary: The US were on the verge of losing two straight at home, but second-half goals from Ashley Sanchez and Mallory Swanson saved a draw. It was nearly time for the panic button. Maybe not to press it, but to look at it – to acknowledge that it’s within reach.
body: Then two players who had just returned to the team after long absences turned the tide. Ashley Sanchez and Mallory Swanson, after international scoring droughts of 1,648 days and 801 days, respectively, each scored in the second half to earn a 2-2 draw with the defending World Cup winners.

The result may have avoided the worst-case scenario, but the way it unfolded will give US fans pause. Just 255 days from the 2027 World Cup, the results raise fresh questions ahead of the side’s return to World Cup qualification in late November. But of course, there are caveats. Both teams were missing key players, with the World Cup still nine months away there’s plenty of time to course-correct.

Rather, the matches served as a helpful reminder to what many – including USWNT head coach Emma Hayes – already knew ahead of them: Spain, the top-ranked team in the world, are the first team in decades that can legitimately outclass the US women, who have long been the international standard bearers for the sport.
“They are world-class. We are still in progress,” Hayes said afterward. “I didn’t learn anything I didn’t already know.”

articles.title: ‘Chip on his shoulder’: Brian Flores lawyers condemn racial stereotypes in NFL coaching report
articles.summary: Recruiting report prepared for Raiders’ 2024 search. Lawyers say assessment contains racial stereotypes. Flores sued NFL over discriminatory hiring in 2022. A recently unsealed recruiting report on Brian Flores contains multiple examples of “racial stereotypes” and amounts to unlawful retaliation…
body: The Korn Ferry report, made public on Tuesday and obtained by the Associated Press, lists six strengths and seven weaknesses that Flores’ attorneys say demonstrate the league’s continued reliance on racial stereotypes in hiring and its retaliation against the coach for his lawsuit alleging racial discrimination.

The report, first published by Front Office Sports, was prepared in connection with the Las Vegas Raiders’ head coaching vacancy in 2024. Flores is now the defensive coordinator for the Minnesota Vikings.

“The recently unsealed documents demonstrate two unfortunate, but unsurprising, realities,” attorney Michael J Willemin said in a statement. “First, that Mr Flores’ decision to hold the league and its teams accountable for systemic race discrimination has been met with unlawful retaliation. Second, discrimination continues to play a significant role in the hiring process for NFL Head Coaches, as evidenced by the fact that the candidate profile prepared for the Raiders leans heavily on racial stereotypes.”
Willemin added: “We and Mr Flores are committed to eradicating the institutional racism and retaliation that permeates the league, its teams and their partners.”

articles.title: Saka responds to Arteta's challenge with 'huge impact'
articles.summary: Bukayo Saka responds to the challenge set by Mikel Arteta as he comes off the bench to change the game against Lille in the Champions League.
body: Bukayo Saka responded to the challenge set by Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta as he proved a game-changer in the 3-0 Champions League win over Lille.
The England forward has been told he should aim to score "two or three" goals per game - such was his quality and the expectation from his boss.
Saka did not achieve that tally against the French visitors, but shook off illness to come off the bench and assist Eberechi Eze's strike that made it 2-0, before rolling in his side's third goal.
The 25-year-old has now scored four goals in nine games this season and looks to be taking the next step in his evolution as Arsenal 's key man.

articles.title: ‘I expect more’: Lisandro Martínez hits out at Manchester United hierarchy
articles.summary: Defeat to Atlético Madrid ‘reflects how our club is’ Argentinian says club has not invested enough in players. Lisandro Martínez has hit out at the Manchester United hierarchy, blaming the lack of investment as their dismal start to the season continued.
body: Asked for his appraisal of the night, Martínez said: “Really poor, really poor. I have to control myself a lot but sometimes is a reflection of the mirror of how is our club at the moment.
It is annoying, disappointing coming here and I am not seeing my team trying to get an amazing result here.

“I expect more [investment], 100%. I expect more from our technical director [Jason Wilcox]. I have to be honest, as players we have to do more but it is also important when you make a strong squad to be ready for this kind of night. Last season we did everything, we created the base to create an amazing team.”

United won 12 of 17 games under Michael Carrick last season but during the summer they made only three major signings – Carlos Baleba, Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans – plus the back-up goalkeeper Karl Darlow on a free transfer from Leeds, and have won only twice in all competitions so far this term. They have suffered the worst start to a league campaign in 40 years.

articles.title: Champions League roundup: Tresoldi treble stuns Inter in Club Brugge win
articles.summary: Inter 3-4 Club Brugge; Galatasaray 1-4 Barcelona. Olise sent off as Bayern held 3-3 at Viking Stavanger. Club Brugge and their young forward Nicolò Tresoldi shocked Inter 4-3 at San Siro in the Champions League’s result of the night.
body: A Hakan Calhanoglu foul on Carlos Forbs resulted in a penalty which Tresoldi slotted in just before the half hour. Tresoldi picked up his second after capitalising on a blunder by the Inter keeper Josep Martínez and reacted faster than the Inter defence for the third with a quarter of an hour to go.

Lautaro Martínez had given his team a lifeline just before the break after a move initiated by Marcus Thuram, followed by a Federico Dimarco back-heel assist. The Argentinian then gave the San Siro crowd hope again in the 81st minute by narrowing the score to 3-2, but Romeo Vermant once again exposed Inter’s defensive fragility by adding a fourth goal in the 87th minute. Ange-Yoan Bonny pulled a goal back for the home side in the third minute of stoppage time.

Having lost 2-1 to Real Madrid at the Bernabéu in their opener, Inter remain on zero points and will be under immense pressure to win next week at home against Shakhtar Donetsk. Brugge, who lost at home to Aston Villa on matchday one, will next host the French club Lens.

articles.title: Swans' Eom the target of alleged racism at Millwall
articles.summary: Swansea City head coach Vitor Matos says the lengthy stoppage during their 1-0 win away at Millwall was a result of racist abuse aimed at winger Ji-sung Eom.
body: The South Korea winger was among the Swansea substitutes, and had been warming up on the side of the pitch when the Championship game was brought to a halt.
Referee Edward Duckworth had lengthy discussions with both sets of coaches, during which the game was paused for around seven minutes.
Following the stoppage, an announcement was made over the speakers at The Den confirming there had been alleged chants of racism and that police were working to identify any offenders using CCTV.
Speaking after the game, Matos said it was the 24-year-old who had been the subject of the abuse.

articles.summary: Northern Ireland manager Michael McArdle says their play-off defeat by Portugal is "the start of a new identity" despite their heavy 7-1 aggregate loss.
body: Portugal showed their ruthlessness during the first leg at Inver Park and had a four-goal advantage ahead of the second leg.
Kess Elmore's strike gave Northern Ireland the lead in Portimao, but the home side fought back and won 3-1 on the night.
"I'm really proud with the brave style of play but we have got to be patient moving forward," McArdle told BBC Sport NI.

"It's been a great camp for new players to come in. Now, I feel the profile of players, the energy they are bringing, the effort that they are putting in and the condition that they are in to compete at this level.

articles.title: Rams player suspended for punch & kicker cut by club
articles.summary: The fallout from the Los Angeles Rams' defeat by the Buffalo Bills continues as offensive lineman Alaric Jackson is suspended for punching an opponent while kicker Harrison Mevis is released.
body: The fallout from the Los Angeles Rams' defeat by the Buffalo Bills rumbled on as offensive lineman Alaric Jackson was suspended for punching an opponent while kicker Harrison Mevis has been released.
Jackson was handed a two-game ban by the NFL after he struck Bills linebacker Bradley Chubb following Monday's 37-34 overtime loss.
Chubb was talking to players from both teams near midfield when Jackson approached him and punched him in the jaw.
"It's just emotions, you know what I mean? Emotional game, it was a close game," Chubb said.

articles.title: Potter’s the present, not just the future after impressive England debut
articles.summary: Lexi Potter could not have done more to prove she should not only be in England’s World Cup squad next summer, she could also be in the starting XI.
body: It's a big shout for a player that's only just broken into the England team, but her 60-minute debut against Greece couldn't have gone much better.

"It was really special," the Chelsea midfielder told ITV Sport after the game. "I am very happy and proud. It was a bit of a rush before the game and I lost my phone! I was a bit nervous but once I got on the pitch, I really enjoyed it.
"It was almost a dream come true. As a young girl, it's what you dream of, playing for your country. To make my debut and to be able to start as well is very special."

The 20-year old grew into the game at the King Power Stadium. She broke up attacks, showed her range of passing, allowed Keira Walsh, Georgia Stanway and Lauren James to shine and even had a goal disallowed.

articles.title: Arenas Wins 2026 Supersport World Championship
articles.summary: Consistency takes rookie to the title. Photos by Yamaha. Albert Arenas wrapped up the 2026 FIM Supersport World Championship, clinching the crown with a fourth-place finish in Race 1 at Estoril.
body: Consistency rather than outright pace carried the title for Arenas, who scored just three victories, taking his maiden win in only his second outing back at Phillip Island before adding further victories at Balaton Park and Misano. Arenas landed on the podium 16 times across 21 races, including 11 runner-up finishes. He retired from three races, and in the races he finished, his lowest result was a single fifth-place result in Race 1 at Algarve. In a season that produced a record nine different race winners, that was enough to bulldoze a field that included quicker outright rivals like Valentin Debise, who sits second on the Zxmoto 820RR-RS.

"Starting from the very first race, where we fought for the lead and then won in the second race, we have been able to be so consistent throughout the season, fighting for wins when we could or the podium or best result possible when not," said Arenas. "I am so happy with this achievement."

Arenas joins Dominique Aegerter, Andrea Locatelli, Sandro Cortese, and Cal Crutchlow as riders who have won the Supersport title in their first full season. He did it despite limited winter testing and being new to the Yamaha R9.

"I have to control myself a lot, but sometimes it's a reflection of how our club is at the moment," Martinez told Amazon Prime.

articles.title: McIlroy: LIV Golf was half a good idea
articles.summary: Rory McIlroy believes LIV Golf was "half a good idea, executed poorly" and the breakaway is no longer a threat to the traditional game as it tries to relaunch after filing for bankruptcy.
body: Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund (PIF) ploughed in £3.7bn over four years, luring the likes of Jon Rahm and Bryson DeChambeau away from the PGA Tour, before withdrawing its support this year.

That led to Chapter 11 bankruptcy proceedings in the United States with a view to relaunching as LIV 2.0, having received a potential $300m (£227m) backing from BC Partners Capital providing a specified number of players re-sign for the new venture.

Rahm has already announced he will not be continuing and news this week that any player signing up for LIV will be barred from DP World Tour membership and Ryder Cup eligibility has delivered a crippling blow.

"LIV had probably like, half of a good idea that was executed pretty poorly," McIlroy told the Bloomberg New Economy forum in New Delhi, where he is playing this week in the DP World India Championship.
